name: de Havilland DH.82 Tiger Moth
summary: British primary-trainer biplane that taught tens of thousands of pilots to fly in World War II; hundreds are still flown worldwide.

wings: Staggered single-bay biplane with a swept-back upper wing over a straighter lower wing
Ailerons on the lower wings only
engines: Inverted inline four-cylinder de Havilland Gipsy engine with a long, low cowled nose
fuselage: Two open cockpits in tandem with fold-down side doors
Fixed split-axle gear with a tailwheel or skid
tail: Large rounded fin and rudder with a tailplane

tellTales: Biplane with a swept-back upper wing and ailerons only on the lower wings
Low inline-engine nose with two tandem open cockpits
Narrow-track fixed gear and rounded tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stampe has ailerons on all four wing panels; the Tiger Moth has ailerons on the lower wings only.
The Jungmann has ailerons on both upper and lower wings and a stubbier, smoother nose; the Tiger Moth has lower-wing ailerons only.
The Stearman has a big radial engine; the Tiger Moth has a slim inline engine nose.
